# AI Waste Sorter

My final year project (BEng Electronic Engineering & Computer Science, Aston University, 2026).

A Raspberry Pi watches a conveyor belt through a camera. A YOLOv8n model I trained on my own dataset spots each item and labels it **metal, plastic or paper**. When the item reaches the trigger line, the Pi fires the matching solenoid to push it into the right bin.

| Metal | Plastic | Paper  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| ![Metal can detected](docs/metal.jpg)![][image1] | ![Plastic bottle detected](docs/plastic.jpg)![][image2] | ![Paper detected and sorted](docs/paper.jpg)![][image3] |

Running live on the Raspberry Pi at about **3.7 FPS** for the whole pipeline (camera → detection → solenoid).

## How it works

```
Camera ──► YOLOv8n (on the Pi) ──► is the item past the trigger line? ──► solenoid for that class fires
                                                                    └─► belt motor (TB6612FNG over I2C)
```

- **Detection:** Ultralytics YOLOv8n, trained on a combined dataset of 3 classes, then exported to NCNN so it runs faster on the Pi's CPU  
- **Control:** `gpiozero` drives three solenoids (GPIO 10, 9, 11 on my build); the belt motor runs through a TB6612FNG driver over I2C  
- **Timing:** each item triggers once when it crosses a set point in the frame (`--trigger_x`), with a cooldown so the same item can't fire twice

## Hardware

- Raspberry Pi \+ Pi Camera (a USB webcam also works)  
- 3 × solenoid actuators and a driver circuit  
- DC belt motor \+ TB6612FNG motor driver

## Repo layout

| Folder / file | What's in it |
| :---- | :---- |
| `sort.py` | Main program: detection \+ solenoid and motor control |
| `my_model/` | Trained model |
| `training/` | Training notebook and the scripts I used to clean, balance and check the dataset |
| `hardware_tests/` | Small scripts for testing the camera, motor and solenoids on their own |

## Run it

```sh
pip install ultralytics opencv-python gpiozero raspberry-i2c-tb6612fng
```

This is the exact command I used for live sorting on the Pi:

```sh
python sort.py --model=my_model/my_modelvn_ncnn_model --source=picamera0 --resolution 640x480 \
  --motor_enable --motor_channel A --motor_speed 105 \
  --solenoid_pins "10,9,11" --solenoid_map "metal:0,plastic:2,paper:1" \
  --pulse_ms 150 --cooldown_ms 800 --min_area 0 --restart_delay_ms 1000
```

Other useful options: `--thresh` (confidence, default 0.5), `--trigger_x` (where the trigger line sits, as a fraction of frame width), `--source usb0` for a USB webcam.

## Training

The biggest problem I hit was class imbalance: about 70% of labelled objects were paper, so the model kept calling plastic and metal "paper". I fixed it by cleaning up labels that didn't match an image, rebalancing the classes and retraining.

## Credits

The training notebook and the base detection script are adapted from EdjeElectronics' [Train-and-Deploy-YOLO-Models](https://github.com/EdjeElectronics/Train-and-Deploy-YOLO-Models) tutorial. The dataset work, the solenoid and motor control, the trigger logic and the hardware are my own.

## What I'd do next

- Build a sturdier conveyor  
- Use stronger solenoids so heavier items get pushed off reliably  
- Train on more varied lighting and backgrounds, so detection doesn't depend on the room it's in  
- Add more classes, like glass and cardboard
